Eliza Grant (Rivermark): Hey team — onboarding hit a weird flap during our traffic ramp. After ~60s we started seeing 403s then a flood of 429s. Errors in app logs show 'token_revoked' then 'quota_exceeded: per_key'. Not sure why tokens are being revoked mid-ramp.
Priya Khatri: Thanks Eliza. Quick context: are you using our SDK directly or a custom auth service? Any autoscaling or job restarts in your infra?
Eliza Grant (Rivermark): We're using the Node SDK v2.2.1 behind our k8s ingress + a small auth sidecar that mints short-lived tokens (TTL 90s). We recently enabled our horizontal pod autoscaler (HPA) to scale the auth sidecar from 1->5 pods during ramp.
Noah Rivera: HPA scaling could cause a stampede of token refreshes if new pod instances all try to warm and request fresh tokens simultaneously. That would create a burst of distinct token issuance attempts for the same API key, and our per_key quota can trigger if many introspects happen in a short window.
Eliza Grant (Rivermark): We do warm logic where each new auth pod prefetches tokens for its worker threads. That probably means 5x the normal issuance during the scale event.
Priya Khatri: Can you paste the auth sidecar config around refresh behavior? Small snippet is fine.
Eliza Grant (Rivermark): Sure: ```yaml
refresh_ttl: 90
refresh_margin_sec: 20
prefetch_per_instance: 10
startup_prefetch: true
```
Noah Rivera: startup_prefetch=true + prefetch_per_instance=10 is likely the cause. When HPA adds 4 pods, you get 40 simultaneous token mints/introspects. If the client then retries aggressively on a small 403 window, that can cascade into per_key quota.
Priya Khatri: Two-part mitigation: 1) ask them to temporarily disable startup_prefetch or lower prefetch_per_instance to 1 while we validate; 2) we can enable a short TEMP_PERKEY_GRACE on the account during the onboarding scale event so they don't get throttled while reconfiguring.
Eliza Grant (Rivermark): We can change prefetch_per_instance to 1 now. Concern: existing pods already prefetched; is there a way to clear or stagger those?
Noah Rivera: You can roll the sidecar deployment with maxSurge: 1 so pods come up one-at-a-time and prefetching is spread out. Alternatively, set startup_prefetch=false and let tokens generate on demand.
Priya Khatri: We'll also monitor introspection logs for your API key around 3500000000-3500000400 to confirm the burst pattern. I'll enable TEMP_PERKEY_GRACE for 2 hours now.
CS Bot: Ticket created: CS-12987 — labels: onboarding, auth, rate-quota. TEMP_PERKEY_GRACE applied until 3500007200. Attachment: initial logs from Eliza.
Eliza Grant (Rivermark): Rolled the auth sidecar with startup_prefetch=false and prefetch_per_instance=1, using maxSurge=1. Will ramp again in 10m.
Noah Rivera: After you ramp, check for residual client retries — if your app's retry policy retries immediately on 403 with no backoff, that can still trigger 429s even with fewer prefetches. Add jittered backoff (start 100ms, jitter up to 200ms).
Eliza Grant (Rivermark): Good call — our retry policy was aggressive (3 attempts, backoff 50ms). I'll increase it to 3 attempts, start 200ms, jitter 100ms.
Priya Khatri: Quick hypothesis summary for the ticket: concurrent HPA pods + startup prefetch caused a token mint/introspect burst; client aggressive retries post-403 amplified the hit and triggered per_key quota. Recommended fixes: stagger startup, disable prefetch, lower prefetch_per_instance, add retry jitter/backoff. We'll add a short note to the onboarding playbook about autoscaler-driven prefetch stampedes.
Eliza Grant (Rivermark): Re-ran ramp after config changes — 20m steady with no 403/429s. The TEMP_PERKEY_GRACE covered the first noisy minutes. Thanks for the quick help.
Noah Rivera: I'll attach the introspection histogram showing the burst to CS-12987 and add playbook text: "When using autoscalers, avoid aggressive startup prefetch; prefer on-demand issuance or staggered startups."
Priya Khatri: Action items: Eliza to continue ramp to full load and confirm, Noah to update ticket with logs and playbook entry, CS to remove TEMP_PERKEY_GRACE after Eliza confirms stability. Also capture this as an enablement talking point for future onboarding calls.
Eliza Grant (Rivermark): Will confirm after 2h of steady traffic. Appreciate the fast turnaround! :raised_hands:
